findings.summary: OAuth callback query values are copied into the request log's status field.
findings.evidence: Probe A: captured logger arguments contain synthetic code/state. server.py log_message uses args[0], the request line, instead of the HTTP status.

findings.summary: A non-1 mutation marker is accepted; GET logout revokes a session without the mutation guards.
findings.evidence: Probe A: wrong-marker POST returns 200 and calls the relay once; foreign-Origin GET logout returns 302 and deletes the synthetic session. No command CSRF bypass established.

findings.summary: The standalone note command has no laptop dispatcher.
findings.evidence: Probe B: actual Ledger.submit with dispatch_handlers returns COMMAND_NOT_IMPLEMENTED for note. Retry reason notes are a separate implemented path.

findings.summary: The phone's SSE URL, event listener and cursor differ from the production gateway.
findings.evidence: Probe C: authenticated /api/remote/v1/events/stream returns 404. page.tsx uses that URL and onmessage; server.py serves /api/remote/v1/stream with named event/resync frames and epoch:sequence IDs. Polling fallback bounds impact.

findings.summary: Gateway restart loses the last cached snapshot while the laptop is offline.
findings.evidence: Probe B: cached web_snapshot is present before restart and absent in a new runtime sharing the same SQLite database. Both runtime snapshot_cache and StreamHub snapshot are memory-only.

findings.summary: The public offline snapshot omits the outage start time needed for the specified sin conexion desde display.
findings.evidence: Static trace: StreamHub.read_snapshot_response and GatewayRuntime.web_snapshot expose laptop.online, without offline_since; cachedAt/generatedAt describe cached data rather than the start of an outage.

findings.summary: Abandoned expired sessions and command/Telegram histories lack the required retention pruning.
findings.evidence: Probe B retains one abandoned expired session after creating a fresh session. Inspection of SessionStore, Ledger.history/rows, NotificationOutbox and observed_events storage finds no 90-day retention cleanup; outbox message expiry only changes status.

findings.summary: The producer waits 900 seconds before a stalled-attempt event instead of more than 600 seconds.
findings.evidence: Probe B prints STALL_SECONDS=900; build_events uses elapsed > STALL_SECONDS. R10 specifies more than 10 minutes.

findings.summary: Quota alerts fire for an exhausted account while another account remains available.
findings.evidence: Probe B: one row with exhausted_until and another available row still produce quota.exhausted; R10 requires every account to be out of quota.

findings.summary: Failure notifications lack cause, review link and inline actions; Telegram retry is unsupported.
findings.evidence: Probe B: notification_for_event drops a synthetic failure cause and contains no review link. TelegramSender sends only chat_id/text. Probe C and app.py restrict Telegram commands to pause/resume.

findings.summary: Telegram /estado reads req_id while the real remote snapshot supplies req.
findings.evidence: Static producer/consumer trace: bt_remote_snapshot emits req; TelegramBot._send_status reads req_id. A focused synthetic native-dialect call to the actual _send_status exits 0 and produces only 'Ejecuciones activas:' with no REQ or reply_markup for an active run. Native snapshot tests exercise the actual producer.

findings.summary: Synchronous Telegram delivery can delay the five-second health and feed polling cycle.
findings.evidence: GatewayRuntime.poll_once calls deliver_due synchronously; NotificationOutbox sends up to 20 messages serially and the default sender timeout is 5 seconds. A 100-second timeout budget is arithmetic, not a measured production outage.

findings.summary: An explicitly empty gateway bind is accepted and means a wildcard HTTP listener.
findings.evidence: Probe B: GatewayConfig.from_env with GATEWAY_BIND='' succeeds with bind_host=''; main.py passes that value directly to ThreadingHTTPServer. No public deployment exposure is claimed.

findings.summary: The default upstream command deadline is five seconds instead of the specified fifteen.
findings.evidence: Probe B prints request_timeout=5.0; GatewayRuntime supplies it to LaptopClient for command POSTs. SPEC's suspended-mid-command case specifies 15 seconds.

findings.summary: Quoted credential fields and database URL passwords survive text-log redaction.
findings.evidence: Probe B: redact leaves synthetic JSON text containing FLOW_GATEWAY_KEY and a postgres password URL unchanged. Structured secret-key dictionaries and ordinary assignment/bearer redaction are distinct, working paths. No real secret was read.

findings.summary: A malformed authenticated command can raise KeyError before deliberate validation.
findings.evidence: Probe B: Ledger.submit for pause with a valid synthetic key but no target raises KeyError in fingerprint before validate. The POST boundary does not translate that exception to INVALID_COMMAND.

findings.summary: The published command schema disagrees with production command fields and limits.
findings.evidence: Static contract/consumer comparison: schema omits answer-decision, uses string route and brief, and permits 128-character keys; the phone sends route objects and field/value, while the native ledger caps keys at 120. JSON syntax is not semantic compatibility evidence.

findings.summary: The phone discards the exact command envelope after UNKNOWN_OUTCOME and uses a new key on resubmission.
findings.evidence: Static page.tsx sendCommand/commandForm trace: HTTP 503 is labeled Rechazado, only a summary enters history and form submitters create another crypto.randomUUID. Server-side same-key replay remains implemented; a specific duplicate effect was not reproduced.

findings.summary: The phone's brief editor prefills the title and has no acceptance-criteria editor.
findings.evidence: Static page.tsx briefForm trace: textarea defaultValue is task.title; submission sends field=objective with a string, and no criteria control exists. Passing native edit-alias tests do not add the missing UI. Silent publication of a title-only objective is not claimed.

findings.summary: Cancel/delete plan controls require a challenge ID without obtaining one in that UI flow.
findings.evidence: Static page.tsx plan controls require confirmation to be nonempty before enabling submit. sendCommand auto-issues a challenge only when challengeId is absent, so the manually required ID prevents that path.

findings.summary: The run-level reopen form omits the task identity required by the laptop operation.
findings.evidence: Static page.tsx Reabrir ejecucion uses kind=run with no taskId; bt_remote_commands TASK_SCOPED/_member_state and dispatch_run_command require params.task for reopen. The separate task-level reopen regression passes.

findings.summary: Route listing considers unknown quota available while pinned retry refuses it.
findings.evidence: Static comparison: bt_remote_recovery.available accepts quota_status != exhausted; bt_route_pins.usable requires quota_status == available. Both operate on the Scheduler candidate source.

findings.summary: Command rate limiting is keyed by login rather than by session as specified.
findings.evidence: The passing gateway test_command_quota_is_shared_by_owner_across_sessions demonstrates the actual behavior; server.py acquires the command limit using owner rather than token. This is stricter aggregate throttling, not authorization bypass.

findings.summary: An existing SSE connection continues receiving events after its session is revoked.
findings.evidence: Probe C: open an authenticated native stream, delete its session, publish an event; the existing stream still returns event: event. Authentication is checked only before entering the stream loop.

findings.summary: The fresh-host runbook restarts the gateway before installing its systemd service.
findings.evidence: Static runbook/deploy.sh trace: Step 3 switches current and invokes systemctl restart; Step 4 installs the unit. Fresh installations cannot complete that restart in the documented order.

findings.summary: The runbook reloads Docker-hosted Caddy through a host systemd service.
findings.evidence: Static runbook Step 5 explicitly says Caddy runs in Docker, but its publish and rollback commands use sudo systemctl reload caddy. No host service was changed.

findings.summary: A missing production frontend gateway origin silently falls back to loopback.
findings.evidence: remote/web/next.config.ts unconditionally defaults FLOW_GATEWAY_ORIGIN to http://127.0.0.1:8790, including production builds. No misconfigured live deployment is asserted.

findings.summary: The integrated browser regression fails while checking the failure-review heading.
findings.evidence: cd remote/web && npm run verify exits 1: lint/typecheck pass; 14/15 tests pass, zero skips. panel-browser.test.mjs:270 fails 'real failure review should render CAUSA'. The earlier 360px width assertion passes in this run. Cause/routing timing is unresolved; product data loss is not inferred.

findings.summary: The local end-to-end test has an unresolved intermittent Telegram message-count failure.
findings.evidence: First full E2E exits 1 after a successful production build: test_local_e2e.py:470 reports 2 != 1 Telegram messages. One diagnostic rerun, preserving the assertions and only adding failure logging, exits 0 (1 test, 21.245s). The extra message's identity was not recovered; neither duplicate-delivery root cause nor a stable clean E2E is claimed.

findings.summary: The previously omitted snapshot/projection and edit/pin modules are present in installed distributions and the installed snapshot executes.
findings.evidence: 2026-10-21 on ddcad27cfc3478f16b366ca15915124ac58b36af: report Probe D exits 0, checks all five modules in fresh wheel and sdist, then runs test_snapshot_uses_shared_now_frame_and_exposes_rejected_review_attempt in an isolated installed interpreter: 1 test passes in 1.098s; every imported bt_ module resolves inside installed.site. The 63-test native suite separately passes installed health.

findings.summary: A stale retry no longer cancels a newer attempt dispatched after its initial precondition read.
findings.evidence: 2026-10-21 on ddcad27cfc3478f16b366ca15915124ac58b36af: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=skill/scripts:skill/scripts/tests python -m unittest test_remote_commands.EntryPointTests.test_f31_route_post_rejects_stale_retry_after_scheduler_starts_new_attempt test_remote_commands.EntryPointTests.test_f32_native_http_rejects_cancel_attempt_that_progressed_after_precondition_read -v exits 0 (2 tests, 0.734s). The F31 regression asserts HTTP 409 STALE_PRECONDITION and that the newer attempt remains dispatched. Independent Probe E also gets 409 with the task still active; its residual pin mutation is F33, not a renewed cancellation claim.

findings.summary: Cancel-attempt rechecks the attempt state under Scheduler ownership before cancellation.
findings.evidence: 2026-10-21 on ddcad27cfc3478f16b366ca15915124ac58b36af: the same explicit two-test command in F31 exits 0. The F32 real HTTP regression advances dispatched to running between the initial read and dispatch, gets HTTP 409 STALE_PRECONDITION, preserves running, records REJECTED and asserts no kill_agent call. The complete native suite also exits 0 (63 tests).

findings.summary: A stale retry still changes the durable route pin before returning STALE_PRECONDITION.
findings.evidence: Probe E exits 0 and reproduces HTTP 409 STALE_PRECONDITION, active task, and persisted route-a after rejection. dispatch_run_command writes/clears pins before ops.retry's state check. Scheduler adapter later consumes bt_route_pins.get/narrow. No newer attempt was cancelled or launched by this rejected command; severity is medium for persistent configuration mutation, not high for the repaired cancellation defect.

findings.summary: The integrated failure-review caller/prop contract typechecks and the production web builds.
findings.evidence: 2026-10-21 on ddcad27cfc3478f16b366ca15915124ac58b36af: npm run verify completes ESLint and tsc before F28; a final standalone cd remote/web && npm run build exits 0 and emits / and /review. The first standalone build overlapped E2E's build and failed ENOENT pages-manifest.json; the final sequential build supersedes only that artifact collision, not the browser failure.

findings.summary: Gateway translation preserves the phone's route/model/account and round/edit fields.
findings.evidence: 2026-10-21 on ddcad27cfc3478f16b366ca15915124ac58b36af: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=remote/gateway python -m unittest discover -s remote/gateway/tests -q exits 0 (52 tests), including real laptop HTTP relay tests for route objects, round answers and edited field/value. Source _ledger_command agrees with those consumers.

findings.summary: Native brief/criteria editing retains phone aliases and refuses unapproved working-plan drift.
findings.evidence: 2026-10-21 on ddcad27cfc3478f16b366ca15915124ac58b36af: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=skill/scripts python -m unittest discover -s skill/scripts/tests -p 'test_remote*.py' -q exits 0 (63 tests). Recovery tests execute actual objective/acceptance_criteria edits and rebase, and reject drift/review without publishing. The missing phone criteria control remains F19.

findings.summary: Immediate command failures expose raw handler exception text in public command results.
findings.evidence: Static Ledger.submit trace: STATE_UNAVAILABLE returns str(exc)[:300], and handler failures put the same raw text in outcome.error. _submit_command and relay_command forward the result. Public history omits outcomes; no actual live-secret exception was read or demonstrated.

findings.summary: The frozen failure-review command names a missing test module and executes no tests.
findings.evidence: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=skill/scripts python -m unittest discover -s skill/scripts/tests -p 'test_remote_review.py' -q exits 5 on Python 3.14: Ran 0 tests / NO TESTS RAN. Existing review assertions in other modules do not make this named check run.

findings.summary: Command activity events use a nonexistent created_at field and get epoch timestamps.
findings.evidence: Actual build_events with a synthetic current Ledger-shaped row containing received_at emits command.updated occurredAt=1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. Producer reads created_at; ledger stores received_at.

findings.summary: Dropped Telegram delivery history is not exposed through public command history or the phone.
findings.evidence: Static storage/route trace: NotificationOutbox.history stores dropped status, but read_routes forwards commands/history to the laptop Ledger.history, which has no Telegram outbox/history join. No public delivery-history route or phone consumer exists. Internal delivery tests pass and do not establish the specified no-entregado display.

findings.summary: The native quota endpoint returns array windows and ISO timestamps that the phone's quota parser discards.
findings.evidence: Focused _quotas call with patched synthetic quota source exits 0 and returns HTTP 200, windows=list and observedAt=ISO string. Static consumer trace: recovery-panels.tsx QuotasPanel requires record(account.windows), snake_case window fields and numeric timestamps. Its record rejects arrays, so native account rows are dropped despite mock-based quota tests passing.

findings.summary: Anonymous users behind the configured reverse proxy share one login rate-limit bucket.
findings.evidence: Fresh Anthropic source hypothesis independently confirmed using actual gateway HTTP: six requests with distinct synthetic X-Forwarded-For clients yield 302,302,302,302,302,429. server.py keys login-start/login on client_address[0]; tracked Caddy reverse_proxy makes that peer shared. Existing sessions remain usable; no trusted-forwarded-header repair or live attack is claimed.

findings.summary: Retrying a terminal task reaches the long retry wait while holding the global command-effect lock.
findings.evidence: A real Scheduler fixture completed via Harness.finish_and_accept, followed by Ledger.submit with the actual retry handler and matching completed/revision precondition, reaches ops.retry sleep(2) while _EFFECT_LOCK cannot be acquired nonblocking. The probe instruments sleep and stops immediately; the production default wait=180 is source evidence, not a measured stall. Other commands share that lock across runs. The provider's ordinary live-cancel path was not reproduced: real cancel moves the task immediately to recovering.
